title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
This is an operational envelope failure. The vehicles stopped when their batteries were exhausted, and because they were driverless, nothing on board could move them out of the roadway. The failure sits in the fleet's energy and traffic management, not in the driving task itself, since the cars are reported to have halted rather than collided.

It happened on public streets during a holiday event that brought heavy traffic and unexpected road closures. Catching it would have required modelling prolonged low-speed congestion and unplanned closures against battery range, or live monitoring able to reroute or recover a vehicle before it came to rest in a travel lane. The company's own account places the conditions outside what the fleet was prepared for.

What is not established is whether the company knew of the limitation beforehand, whether any rule or permit condition was breached, or what caused the fire beyond the reported account of a vehicle driving over fireworks. The mayor's office announced conversations about future traffic management, which is a stated intention and not a finding.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets after their batteries died during heavy traffic following Fourth of July fireworks celebrations on Saturday. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets, with some requiring towing assistance. The company attributed the incident to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unexpected road closures. Waymo stated its roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles and indicated the company is evaluating ways to improve its resilience during severe traffic events.

The incident also involved a Waymo vehicle that caught fire after driving over fireworks set off in the street, though no injuries were reported. Witnesses described frustration as people exited their cars to yell at the driverless vehicles stuck in traffic. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to have conversations with public and private partners to ensure smoother traffic management for future events in the city.
